body.statement:
For \(1<s\le2\), under the unchanged class \(\mathcal P_n\) and the detectable-region condition \(T_n\gtrsim\log(e/\kappa_n)\), determine whether there are constants \(0<c<C<\infty\), depending only on \(s,M,v,\alpha\), such that
\[
 c\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}+\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\right\}
 \le L_n(\kappa_n)\le
 C\min\left\{1,\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}+\frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\right\}.
\]
The upper side must use the degree-one profile localization in def:profile-cutoff-center and complete the fold-four bias-aware inversion.  The converse must construct matching slope-kink pairs in \(\mathcal P_n\).  In particular, prove or refute that the known-cutoff order \(\rho_n/\kappa_n\) is attained precisely on the face where \(n\kappa_n^2\rho_n\) is bounded below by a positive constant.  No cross-side derivative-matching condition may be added.
body.justification: The question records the exact same-class rate bracket left after localization is solved and exposes the required upper and lower constructions.
body.gap: Neither a uniform fold-four bound for the \(MR_c/\kappa_n\) term nor a matching slope-kink lower pair is yet proved.
body.consumer: Its resolution will tell higher-smoothness applications when unknown-cutoff uncertainty is negligible relative to known-cutoff weak-LATE uncertainty.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform higher-smoothness fold-four length upper bound with the \(MR_c/\kappa_n\) term and a matching same-class slope-kink lower pair.
obligation.obstruction: The profile center now localizes at \(R_c\asymp(n\kappa_n^2)^{-1}\), but separate one-sided H\"older extensions allow the transformed-outcome derivative to kink at the cutoff. Moving the center by \(R_c\) therefore creates order \(MR_c/\kappa_n\), and no frozen lower construction yet certifies that this term is necessary.
obligation.attempted: The raw intercept-jump scan was replaced by a degree-one profile score. Orthogonal projection of the step indicator against \(1,u,(u-q)_+\) proves population separation and a sequential Bernstein argument proves the desired localization tail. Propagating this tail through fixed-center inversion exposes, rather than removes, the additional \(1/(n\kappa_n^3)\) term.
obligation.partial_result:
The profile identity already closes the localization component without derivative matching: for \(|q|\le1/2\), the residualized step satisfies \(\lVert k_q\rVert_2^2=(1-q^2)/8\ge3/32\), and the slope-kink regressor \((u-q)_+\) is projected out.  The resulting center has conditional tail
\[
 P\{|\hat c_{\mathrm{prof}}-c_P|>u,\mathcal E_{\mathrm p}\}
 \le64\exp\{-2^{-30}m\kappa_n^2u\}.
\]
Thus its natural error is \(R_c\asymp(n\kappa_n^2)^{-1}\).  For the transformed-outcome jump, the unchanged class permits a derivative kink, so moving the center by \(R_c\) contributes order \(MR_c/\kappa_n\asymp(n\kappa_n^3)^{-1}\) to LATE length, in addition to the known-cutoff term \(\rho_n/\kappa_n\).  The equality
\[
 \frac1{n\kappa_n^3}\lesssim\frac{\rho_n}{\kappa_n}
 \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad n\kappa_n^2\rho_n\gtrsim1
\]
explains the proposed oracle face.  What remains open is a uniform fold-four upper proof with this radius and an in-class slope-kink lower pair attaining the same second term.
